questions.question: What is a drawback of retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed in all places.
They can help slow a vehicle.
They cannot be turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed in all places.
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, these devices can be loud and are not allowed everywhere.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: Often wrong or misleading.
The only way a driver can find out about vehicle problems.
One way to find out about possible vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: One way to find out about possible vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: During a trip, check the gauges and instrument panels regularly. Also check your mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for problems.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are not safe to use.
Are safe to use on rear tires.
Are safe to use if carrying a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are never safe to use.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead of you:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
Is not recommended because it distracts you.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react to problems before you reach them.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: Before driving
While driving
After driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you start driving. If your vehicle has a trailer, it must be straight so you can check the mirrors correctly.

questions.question: In very hot weather, check tires regularly because:

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
The tread wears faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Pay close attention to tire mounting and pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: A surge happens with which type of cargo?

options.text: Solid
Liquid
Gas

questions.correctAnswerText: Liquid
questions.explanation: Tanks carrying liquid cargo can experience surge. This is when liquid waves back and forth inside the tank, which makes the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: Aggressive driving is:

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with strong concern for other drivers' safety.
Driving in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy way without regard for other road users' safety.

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop shortly to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check if rocks are stuck in the tread.
Polish the tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: When pulled off on the side of the road:

options.text: A driver should keep the driver's door open.
A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
The driver should wave their arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: An impaired driver.
A color blind driver.
A driver who does not know traffic rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired. Drivers who drink alcohol, are tired, use drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign is stopping at places they should not stop, like at green lights.

questions.question: Water on a roadway can cause:

options.text: Hydroplaning.
Acceleration.
Stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road surface.

questions.question: When using controlled braking with liquid cargo, you should brake:

options.text: Gently to keep the wheels rolling.
Hard enough to lock up the wheels.
As hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: As hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep small movements with the steering wheel when braking this way.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving a vehicle with the intent to harm others.
Driving a vehicle that is not safe.
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving a vehicle with the intent to harm others.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means driving in a selfish, bold, or pushy way. Road rage means driving with the intent to hurt others or their vehicles, or to physically harm another driver.

questions.question: If shipping papers list both hazardous and non-hazardous materials:

options.text: Hazardous materials must be listed first.
Hazardous materials must be written larger.
Hazardous materials must be in red ink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials must be listed first.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, put the hazardous materials first.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, reduce your speed by:

options.text: One-half or more.
About one-third.
About one-quarter.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-half or more.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed on surfaces with poor grip. On packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The nuts are too tight.
The nuts are loose.
The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts shows they may be loose. Check that wheel nuts are tight if you see rust near them before driving.

questions.question: When driving, you should keep in mind:

options.text: How far your vehicle needs to stop.
What time you should arrive.
How many cars are ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: How far your vehicle needs to stop.
questions.explanation: Safe driving means knowing your stopping distance. Stopping distance changes with road and weather conditions, and how full your vehicle's tanks are.

questions.question: In cold temperatures, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other road surfaces.
Before other road surfaces.
At the same time as other road surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: In cold weather, bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Be extra careful on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: Baffled liquid tanks are:

options.text: Tanks that control liquid surge with perforated bulkheads.
Tanks with no bulkheads that let liquids move freely.
Tanks with nothing inside to slow liquid flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tanks that control liquid surge with perforated bulkheads.
questions.explanation: Baffled liquid tanks have bulkheads with holes that let liquid move while slowing down forward and backward surge. They do not stop side-to-side surge and can still cause rollovers.
